chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them):

That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was met by a Bedouin who said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, I set out intending to perform Hajj, but I was prevented, and I am a man of means. Order me to do with my wealth what will bring me the same reward as the pilgrim.' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned to him and said to him: "Look at Abu Qubays [the mountain near Mecca]. If Abu Qubays were gold for you, red gold, and you spent it in the way of Allah, you would not reach with it what the pilgrim reaches."'

Then he said: 'Indeed, when the pilgrim prepares his gear, he raises nothing and places nothing except that Allah writes for him ten good deeds, erases ten bad deeds, and raises him ten degrees. When he mounts his camel, he lifts not a hoof nor places it except that Allah writes for him the like of that. When he circumambulates the House, he goes forth from his sins. When he runs between Safa and Marwa, he goes forth from his sins. When he stands at Arafat, he goes forth from his sins. When he stands at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, he goes forth from his sins. When he throws the pebbles at the Jamarat, he goes forth from his sins.'
He said: 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) enumerated so many and so many stations; whenever the pilgrim stands at them, he goes forth from his sins.'

Then he said: 'How can you reach what the pilgrim reaches?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And sins are not written against him for four months, and good deeds are written for him, unless he commits a major sin.'

key_terms.أَبُو قُبَيْسٍ: Abu Qubays (a mountain near Mecca, used as a measure of volume/size)
key_terms.خَرَجَ مِنْ ذُنُوبِهِ: Freed from his sins / sins erased
key_terms.رَجُلٌ مُمِيلٌ: A man of means / wealthy man
key_terms.وَقَفَ: Stood (at the station of Arafat or Muzdalifah)

ai.seo_question: How does the reward of Hajj compare to spending wealth for those who cannot travel?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique, action-specific merit of Hajj, where each physical station—from preparing gear to stoning the Jamarat—generates distinct divine rewards, distinguishing it from general charity. The Prophet (SAWW) clarifies that while wealth cannot replicate this cumulative spiritual elevation, the pilgrim enjoys a four-month period of suspended sins (provided no major sin is committed), a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the purification of the soul through ritual presence.
